text: Why are GPUs the default hardware for training large neural networks, even though they were built for graphics?
options: Because they accelerate the linear algebra involved
Because they have fast serial integer arithmetic
Because they use very little power per computation
Because they have large caches for text corpora
answer: Because they accelerate the linear algebra involved
explanation: Every layer of a neural network is a matrix multiply, and GPUs are thousands of cores doing the same operation on thousands of elements at once. Drawing triangles turned out to be the same shape of problem, which is one of the luckiest accidents in the history of computing.

text: Which Google chip is an application specific integrated circuit built specifically for neural network workloads?
explanation: Google started using TPUs internally in 2015 and opened them to third parties through its cloud in 2018. TensorFlow, JAX and PyTorch all support them, and the distinction from an NPU is mostly that Google calls its own product a TPU.

Nvidia created it in 2004 and released it in 2007, and it is a platform and API rather than a chip. It is also the reason Nvidia is hard to displace, since the software ecosystem built on it is decades deep and a competitor has to beat the hardware and the tooling at once.

text: High Bandwidth Memory stacks DRAM dies vertically. Which three companies first developed the standard?
explanation: It is a 3D stacked SDRAM interface, and the first HBM chip came from SK Hynix in 2013. Training is frequently memory bandwidth bound rather than compute bound, which is why the HBM supply chain became a chokepoint for the whole industry within about two years.

text: Nvidia's Hopper microarchitecture is designed primarily for which workload?
explanation: Hopper is a datacenter part and sits alongside Lovelace, which is the consumer line. The name comes from Grace Hopper, the naval rear admiral, and the H100 built on it is the chip most of the 2023 to 2025 training runs were done on.

text: Nvidia's Ampere GPU microarchitecture is named after which person?
explanation: The French physicist and mathematician after whom the ampere is named, and Nvidia announced Ampere in May 2020. Nvidia does this consistently, since Blackwell, Hopper and Ampere are all people, and the convention is one of the easier ways to place a card in a timeline.

text: Which company builds the wafer scale engine, a processor built by linking many dies across a single silicon wafer?
explanation: Cerebras in Sunnyvale, California builds a processor the size of a wafer and the CS-3 supercomputers around it, and sells access by API as well. The bet is that model parallelism beats the difficulty of getting a single enormous chip manufactured reliably.

text: An NPU, also called an AI accelerator, is best described as what?
options: A general purpose CPU with a wider instruction set
A type of DRAM stacked in three dimensions
A compiler that targets GPUs instead of CPUs
A specialised hardware accelerator for AI workloads
answer: A specialised hardware accelerator for AI workloads
explanation: It can be standalone, part of a CPU or part of a GPU, and the term is a category rather than a product. The whole category grew out of the observation that neural network inference does a small number of operations very many times, which is a different shape of problem from general purpose computing.

text: Moore's law says the number of transistors on an integrated circuit does what over time?
options: Doubles roughly every two years at near constant cost
Halves roughly every five years at rising cost
Triples every decade at falling cost
Doubles every decade at constant cost
answer: Doubles roughly every two years at near constant cost
explanation: Moore published it as an observation in 1965, not a law, and it described an empirical relationship rather than a physical necessity. It is also the reason people believed AI scaling would be affordable, since compute was on an exponential curve even when the models were not yet good enough to use.

text: Nvidia was founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang and two co-founders. What were the other two names?
explanation: The three founded Nvidia after leaving Sun Microsystems, and the company nearly ran out of money in its first few years. Jensen Huang is the one who stayed famous enough to be the answer to a different question, which is the last question on the founders list.

text: Which foundry manufactures most of Nvidia's AI chips and was founded in 1987 by Morris Chang?
explanation: TSMC pioneered the pure-play foundry model and fabs Nvidia's datacenter GPUs, including Blackwell on its 4NP process. Samsung is the tempting miss because it also fabs advanced chips, but Nvidia's AI lineup runs overwhelmingly through TSMC.

text: Which company is the sole supplier of extreme ultraviolet lithography machines for advanced chips?
explanation: The Dutch firm ASML holds a near-monopoly on EUV systems printing 5 nm and 3 nm layers at 13.5 nm wavelength. Nikon is the tempting miss because it once led lithography with Canon, but neither ships EUV machines today.

text: Nvidia's Blackwell architecture is named after which person?
explanation: David Blackwell was the statistician behind game theory and probability work that underpins modern ML, honored at GTC 2024 with the B200 datacenter accelerators. Grace Hopper is the tempting miss because Hopper is the preceding Nvidia architecture, also named for a person.

text: Which Nvidia chip became the workhorse of AI training during the 2022 to 2024 boom?
explanation: The Hopper-based H100 powered most frontier training runs of the boom, succeeding the Ampere A100. The A100 is the tempting miss because it was the previous workhorse, but by 2023 waitlists and headlines all pointed at H100 supply.

text: How many GPUs did Nvidia's DGX-1 contain, the system whose first unit was delivered to OpenAI in 2016?
explanation: The DGX-1 packed 8 Pascal P100 GPUs linked by NVLink, and Jensen Huang hand-delivered the first box to OpenAI. Sixteen is the tempting miss because later DGX generations scaled up, but the original 2016 box held eight.

text: What does the LPU in Groq's chip name stand for?
explanation: Groq rebranded its tensor streaming chip as the Language Processing Unit for LLM inference, and its 2024 speed demos went viral. Linear Processing Unit is the tempting miss because it sounds like standard hardware jargon, but the official expansion is Language, which also fueled confusion with xAI's Grok chatbot.
